{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE:
#   Slurm uses a job array (--array=0-2). Flux job arrays are not available as a
#   universally portable batch-script directive.
#
# Run with:
#   flux batch <this_script> -- <TASK_ID>
# where <TASK_ID> is 0, 1, or 2.

# Slurm resources:
#   --job-name=array-job
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks=1
#   --cpus-per-task=1
#   --mem-per-cpu=4G
#   --time=00:01:00
#   --output=slurm-%A.%a.out
#   --error=slurm-%A.%a.err
#   --array=0-2

#flux: --job-name=array-job
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 1
#flux: --time-limit=1m

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem-per-cpu=4G
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on nodes with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --array=0-2
# Flux job arrays are not available as a universally portable batch-script directive.
# Performance implication: you must submit multiple jobs manually (or via a loop), increasing scheduler overhead and potentially reducing throughput.

# Omitted Slurm options: --output/--error with %A/%a tokens
# Slurm tokens %A (array master job id) and %a (array index) are not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

TASK_ID=${1:-0}

echo "My TASK_ID is ${TASK_ID}."
echo "My Flux job id is ${FLUX_JOB_ID:-unknown}."
echo "Executing on the machine: $(hostname)"

module purge
module load anaconda3/2023.9

python myscript.py
"
}
